transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… yeah, thanks. I guess I’m here because I keep getting these flashes, kind of out of nowhere. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s like I’m suddenly back in that crowded holding room—seeing the fight, hearing people getting shoved up against the wall. It can happen when I’m just standing at a pickup counter for work. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… it’s been hard to shake.
What seems to trigger these flashes for you?

Mostly places that feel crowded or kind of… official, I guess. Like when I’m at a pickup counter for work and there are people close together, voices raised, that sort of thing. It’s not like I’m trying to think about it, it just hits me—like I’m back in that holding room, seeing the fight and hearing people getting shoved into the wall. I know that probably sounds like a lot, but that’s the main thing I’ve noticed.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places or situations because of these flashes?

Yeah… I mean, a little. I’ve been trying not to make a big deal out of it, but I have been turning down some night runs, especially if they’d take me near that detention building. I’ll take the long way around town instead, which probably isn’t the smartest for work, but I just… I can’t seem to make myself go near it.

And talking about what happened is hard too. I try to keep it brief, because if I get into it, it feels like I’m right back there again. Is that the kind of avoiding you mean?
Do you have trouble sleeping at night?

Yeah… I mean, it’s not great. I don’t want to sound like I’m falling apart, but I barely sleep now. I’ll doze off for maybe an hour or two, and then I’m up again because of some dream about that cell, or I hear a door slam in the dream and it jolts me awake.

By morning I’m just… wrecked. Like too wiped out to feel okay driving my route sometimes. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself jumping or getting startled easily by loud noises or unexpected movements?

Yeah… I guess I do. I mean, I try not to make it obvious, but every radio crackle or siren or even a door slamming, I just jump like somebody’s about to rush me.

And then it doesn’t pass right away. My heart keeps pounding so hard afterward that sometimes I have to pull over if I’m driving, or step outside for a minute. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but… yeah, that’s been happening.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed about what happened in that holding room?

I… I don’t know. I mean, I don’t think I did anything wrong, exactly. Or at least I’m trying to tell myself that.

Ashamed, maybe… a little. It’s hard to say that out loud. I keep thinking I should’ve handled it better, or not let it get to me so much. But I’m not sure if that’s guilt, or just feeling embarrassed that I wasn’t… tougher, I guess.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do you often find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential threats or dangers?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I’d say I’m constantly looking for danger, exactly. I mean, I’m maybe more aware of things around me than I used to be, but I don’t know if that counts.

Like, I’m not trying to make it sound worse than it is. I just notice stuff sometimes and then try to tell myself it’s nothing. Is that what you mean, or do you mean like actively checking all the time?
Do you have difficulty concentrating on tasks?

Um… I’m not sure. I mean, I can still do things if I really force myself to, so I don’t want to say I can’t concentrate.

Maybe I lose my place a little more than usual, but I haven’t really been keeping track. Are you asking like at work, or just in general?
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest, exactly. I still want to like the things I used to like.

Maybe I haven’t been doing them as much, but I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve just stopped caring about everything. It’s more like… I’m not sure if I’m just tired or distracted or what.

Does that answer it, or are you asking if I don’t enjoy them at all anymore?
Do you often feel like you're on edge, even when there's no apparent reason to be?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say all the time, but I do get kind of jumpy. Like if a radio crackles or there’s a siren, or even just a door slams, I’ll react before I can stop myself.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I jump like something’s about to happen, like I’m about to get rushed or something, and then my heart keeps pounding way longer than it should. Sometimes I have to pull over or step outside for a minute until it settles.

I don’t know if that’s what you mean by “on edge,” but… yeah, I guess that’s been happening.
Do you often think that you're worthless or that you've failed as a person because of what happened in that holding room?

I… I don’t know if I’d say worthless. That sounds pretty strong.

I’ve had moments where I think maybe I should’ve handled it better, or I replay it and wonder what I did wrong, but I’m not sure that’s the same as feeling like I failed as a person. I don’t really want to make it sound bigger than it is.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you stopped doing things you used to enjoy since these flashes started happening?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I haven’t exactly made a decision to stop doing things, if that makes sense.

Some things I just… haven’t gotten around to, or I tell myself I’ll do them later. But I don’t know if that’s because of the flashes specifically, or because I’m just tired and trying to keep things normal.

I still want to be the kind of person who does those things. I don’t want it to sound like I’m just giving up. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed yourself participating less in hobbies or activities that were once important to you?

Yeah… I guess I have, more than I wanted to admit.

It’s not like I stopped caring about those things. I just… I haven’t been showing up. I’ve missed two shifts already, and even when I try to work, I don’t feel right driving or handling deliveries. I feel too shaken, too on edge, and I don’t want to mess something up.

And I’ve kind of stopped going to my volunteer stuff too. I keep telling myself I’ll go next time, but being around people right now feels like too much, like I can’t really keep it together.

I don’t know if that counts as “participating less,” but… yeah, I think it does.
Do you try to avoid thinking about what happened in that holding room?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I try not to make a whole thing out of it, but yes.

I avoid bringing it up, because once I start talking about the holding room it’s like I’m right back there again. And I’ve been… adjusting things, I guess. Turning down night runs, taking the long way around town so I don’t have to go near that detention building.

I know that probably sounds like avoidance. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything. I just can’t seem to make myself go near it or talk about it without it hitting me all over again.
Have you lost interest in things you used to find important or enjoyable?

I don’t know if I’d say I’ve lost interest exactly. I still care about those things, and I’d like to get back to them.

It’s more like… I’m not really reaching for them right now. I keep putting things off or telling myself I’ll feel up to it later. Maybe that sounds like the same thing, I’m not sure. I just don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.
Do you believe that what happened in that holding room has changed you as a person in a lasting way?

I’m not sure I’d say “lasting,” no. I mean… I hope not.

It’s changed how I feel right now, definitely, but saying it changed me as a person feels… I don’t know, too big? I don’t want to overstate it or make it sound like I think I’m broken or something.

Maybe I’m still too close to it to know. Is that an okay answer? Right now it feels different, but I’m not sure I believe it’s permanent.
